messages:
kai: Quick Q — we have a request to change the default model selection for /v1/generate to prefer faster-quantized variants. Before we do anything, want alignment on contract guarantees for unpinned requests.

jess: we should treat unpinned defaults as non-breaking but documented changeable behaviour. customers relying on output distribution is a risk. do we have telemetry on how many clients omit model param?

anika: ~12% of traffic today. mostly small apps. We also saw a spike in eval regressions when we rolled a kernel change in feb.

sam: important: clients expect stable response shape (fields), not necessarily model logits. any change to schema is breaking. changing which model answers is behavior change but we can deprecate.

liz: agree with sam. also need a timeline and a clear header so SDKs can warn. propose: add a response header when default is used: `X-Default-Model: redwood-quant-v1` and include `model_used` in response metadata.

kai: good idea. example request/response I'd like to standardize in the contract:
```http
POST /v1/generate
{ "prompt": "foo", "model": <optional> }
```
Current response shape we guarantee today: 
```json
{ "id": "r_xxx", "object": "text_completion", "model": "redwood-v2", "choices": [{ "text": "...", "index": 0 }], "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 10 } }
```
Proposed additions (non-breaking): add `meta.model_used` and `warnings` array. Proposed breaking: rename `choices[].text` -> `choices[].content` (we should not do that without major version).

jess: +1 to model_used and header. do NOT rename fields. we can introduce aliases but avoid breaking. also we need a deprecation playbook: notice window, SDK warnings, migration guide, canary rollout.

sam: timeline suggestion: 90-day notice for default-model policy changes. During that window: 1) response header + SDK deprecation warning, 2) opt-in feature flag for new default routing, 3) telemetry dashboard for regressions.

anika: operationally, runtime can flip routing by tag. I can add a flag `route.default_model_variant = "quant-v1"` behind `feature.default_model_routing` so canarying is straightforward.

liz: for communications: product will draft a short blog + email. eng should publish an SDK compatibility patch that emits warnings when model param omitted. who owns the SDK PRs?

kai: assign to jess for JS/sdk and sam for python. sam — can you add the header and `meta.model_used` in runtime response? keep it optional until fully rolled.

sam: will do. timeline: header + meta in 2 weeks, feature flag rollout in 4 weeks, deprecation notice on day 1 of rollout.

jess: will open JS PR tomorrow with a console.warn when `model` is undefined; will include pointer to migration guide. link to draft PR: https://git.internal/pr/2345 (pr-bot: referenced).

pr-bot: PR 2345 opened by jess -> https://git.internal/pr/2345 : include changelog entry 'Warn when model param omitted'

deploy-bot: Scheduled runtime change on 1785570000 for header rollout (canary first).

kai: final decisions:
- do not change response field names (no breaking rename)
- add `X-Default-Model` header and `meta.model_used` (non-breaking)
- 90-day deprecation notice before any behavioural guarantee removal
- rollout behind `feature.default_model_routing` + canary
- SDKs to warn when model param omitted

Action items:
- sam: add header + meta in 2w (assigned)
- anika: add runtime flag + routing tag (4w)
- jess: SDK warning PR + changelog (tomorrow)
- liz: draft customer comms + blog (this week)
- kai: write short RFC with timeline and rollback plan (by EOD Friday)

liz: thanks all — will sync with product marketing. :thumbsup:

kai: thanks — closing thread, followups on RFC and PRs.
